questions.ask: A customer was charged twice for $450. Can I just refund it, or do I need to ask someone?
questions.reply: You can approve that yourself. The refund policy says Tier 1 agents may approve duplicate-charge refunds up to $600 without escalation, and it goes back in full within 5 business days once Billing confirms the duplicate. The section is highlighted in the panel.

result.query: duplicate charge refund approve without escalation

results.heading: Duplicate charges
results.text:
## Duplicate charges
A duplicate charge is refunded in full within 5 business days once Billing confirms it. Agents on Tier 1 may approve duplicate-charge refunds up to $600 without escalation.

results.heading: When to escalate
results.text:
## When to escalate
Escalate to Tier 2 when a ticket is a confirmed bug, involves data loss, or has breached its first-response SLA. Escalate to the Escalations team for any urgent ticket older than 4 hours without a resolution or any ticket from an Enterprise customer with CSAT below 3.

questions.ask: When am I supposed to escalate an urgent ticket?
questions.reply: Two triggers from the runbook: any urgent ticket older than 4 hours without a resolution, or any Enterprise customer with CSAT below 3. Set it to escalated, assign an Escalations agent, and don't promise a timeline until Tier 2 has triaged.

result.query: escalate urgent ticket hours escalations team

results.heading: When to escalate
results.text:
## When to escalate
Escalate to Tier 2 when a ticket is a confirmed bug, involves data loss, or has breached its first-response SLA. Escalate to the Escalations team for any urgent ticket older than 4 hours without a resolution or any ticket from an Enterprise customer with CSAT below 3.

results.heading: How to escalate
results.text:
## How to escalate
Set status to escalated, assign to an Escalations agent, and post the ticket link in the escalations channel with the customer's plan and the SLA breach time. Do not promise timelines to the customer before Tier 2 has triaged.

results.heading: Churn risk
results.text:
## Churn risk
A customer with two or more overdue invoices and an open urgent ticket is flagged as churn risk. Account management is notified the same day.

questions.ask: What's the first-response target for a High ticket from a Business-plan customer?
questions.reply: Four business hours for High, and Business-plan customers also get a named escalation contact. The 30-minute target only applies to urgent tickets. Both sections are in the panel with the matching lines highlighted.

result.query: first response target high business hours plan

results.heading: First response targets
results.text:
## First response targets
- Urgent: 1 hour, 24x7
- High: 4 business hours
- Normal: 1 business day
- Low: 2 business days

results.heading: Business and Enterprise plans
results.text:
## Business and Enterprise plans
Business and Enterprise customers get a named escalation contact and a 30-minute urgent first-response target during US business hours.

results.heading: When to escalate
results.text:
## When to escalate
Escalate to Tier 2 when a ticket is a confirmed bug, involves data loss, or has breached its first-response SLA. Escalate to the Escalations team for any urgent ticket older than 4 hours without a resolution or any ticket from an Enterprise customer with CSAT below 3.
